author: Mark Atwood
text: Rust idiom confidence (rusty pass #2): 25% chance of missed issue (DOWN from 30% in rusty pass #1). Confidence improved because the 10 fix commits were each scoped and minimal — easier to read every line than to re-walk the whole crate. Did inspect the diff line-by-line for each fix; did not run cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings against the post-fix tree (workspace policy denies edits/writes in review mode, but I could have done a read-only invocation — that would have raised confidence further). Did NOT file a finding for the new e.to_string() leak introduced at calendar.rs:275 by bdf40aa, even though it matches the JMAP-ic0j.53 anti-pattern and creates a third sibling site (alongside the existing 156/215/326 BackendSetError::Other arms): the leakage concern is correctness/api-contract (review-myoss territory), not idiomatic-rust, AND fixing it requires propagating from the canonical mail-server (which has the same pattern in 30+ sites across email.rs/sieve.rs/mailbox.rs/identity.rs). A workspace-wide bead for per-item BackendSetError::Other leakage might be worth filing under a different epic, but is out of scope for /review-rusty. Least confident: whether the new debug_assert! sites in 4e3cb9f's dedup loop should have been filed as 'idiom violation: assertion on test-mode-only invariant that does not match the assertion's wording' — the assertion text says 'silently drops the create in release builds' which is documenting the bug rather than the invariant; reasonable people could file this as a docs idiom finding, but the assertion text is informative not normative and I'm letting it stand.
